title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Databricks (AWS baseline)
providers.scope_notes: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

controls.name: IP access lists
controls.what: Restrict account console/account APIs and workspace/workspace APIs to approved IPs.
controls.setting: Account console IP access lists; workspace IP Access List API
controls.quote: The default allows connections from any IP address.

controls.name: Context-based ingress policies
controls.what: Account-level allow/deny rules combining identity, network source and request scope, e.g. pinning service principals to trusted networks.
controls.quote: allow and deny rules that combine who is calling, from where they are calling, and what they can reach

controls.name: Service principal OAuth secret lifetime
controls.what: Each OAuth secret gets a lifetime set at creation, max 730 days.
controls.setting: Service principal > Secrets > Generate secret (account or workspace admin)
controls.quote: Set the secret’s lifetime in days (maximum 730 days).

controls.name: OAuth secret scopes
controls.what: Admins choose API scopes when generating a secret; they cannot be changed later.
controls.quote: Scopes are set when you generate the secret and can’t be changed afterward.

controls.name: Deactivate a service principal
controls.what: Deactivated service principals cannot authenticate; their OAuth secrets and tokens stop working until reactivated.
controls.setting: Account Service Principals API (account level); Workspace Service Principals API (workspace level)

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable PATs across all workspaces was found; the toggle is per workspace.
Whether IP access lists explicitly cover PAT/OAuth API calls is implied (workspace-level APIs) but not stated.
Whether context-based ingress rules can distinguish auth method (PAT vs OAuth) is not stated.
How to update or delete federation policies, and how to revoke an individual OAuth secret, were not covered on the fetched pages.
TTL min/max ranges, and whether built-in databricks-cli app follows app-connection TTL defaults, not confirmed.
Single-use refresh token details page returned 404; defaults per app not confirmed.
Azure/GCP capabilities and tiers not checked.

authentication.summary: OAuth user-to-machine and machine-to-machine, external token federation, and legacy personal access tokens.

federation.details: External IdP tokens exchange into Databricks OAuth using configured issuer/audience/subject trust; workload CI/runtime federation supported.

ip_restriction.boundary: Enterprise tier. Separate account/workspace IP lists protect public UI/API access; PrivateLink traffic is not filtered by them. Context-based ingress (Enterprise) can add rules combining identity (e.g. service principal), network source and access type.

renewal.summary: Re-mint a 1-hour access token with the service principal client ID and OAuth secret (SDK/CLI do this automatically). The OAuth secret has a set lifetime of up to 730 days and can be scoped.

administration.summary: Service principals, entitlements/resource ACLs, federation policies, PAT controls and context-based ingress controls.
administration.conditions: AWS IP-access-list docs require Enterprise tier. Azure/GCP capabilities and licensing must be checked separately.

offboard.details: Credential belongs to a service principal, not a user.

inventory.details: OAuth secrets are listed per service principal on its Credentials & secrets tab; no account-wide secret report found.

inventory.ui: Account console > User management > Service principals > <SP> > Credentials & secrets (per SP)

reads.api: SQL: SELECT * FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name='workspace' AND action_name='workspaceExport' (filter user_identity.email)

token_format.notes: Client secret format not documented by Databricks. GitHub scans it as databricks_oauth_secret_token (no push protection). Client ID = service principal application ID.

log_sources.name: Databricks audit logs (system.access.audit system table / audit log delivery)
log_sources.notes: Account- and workspace-level events; account-level rows have workspace_id 0. No general retention stated on the table page; events of a deleted workspace older than 14 days are removed.

log_sources.name: Service principal secrets list API
log_sources.notes: Returns id, secret_hash, status, create_time, expire_time per secret; metadata only.

anomaly_cues: mintOAuthToken for a client_id from a source_ip_address outside the workload's known egress range
new servicePrincipalCredentials.create on a long-lived SP shortly followed by token minting from a new IP
SP secret created by a non-automation admin identity
mintOAuthToken with grant_type client_credentials at unusual volume or hours for a batch SP

containment.steps: Delete the secret (DELETE /api/2.0/accounts/{account_id}/servicePrincipals/{service_principal}/credentials/secrets/{secret_id}); to stop tokens already minted, deactivate the service principal via the Account Service Principals API, then rotate.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether deleting a secret invalidates issued access tokens (1-hour lifetime). SP deactivation blocks all its tokens.

sample_query.query: SELECT event_time, request_params['client_id'] AS client_id, source_ip_address, user_agent, response.statusCode FROM system.access.audit WHERE service_name = 'accounts' AND action_name = 'mintOAuthToken' AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 30 DAYS AND request_params['client_id'] = '<sp-application-id>' ORDER BY event_time DESC
sample_query.purpose: See where and how often a service principal mints OAuth tokens

unknown: whether deleting a secret revokes issued access tokens
which secret_id was used to mint a given token (mintOAuthToken params list no secret_id)

calls.reveals: Notebook or whole-directory contents (source code, sometimes embedded secrets/results)
calls.log_notes: Audit log / system.access.audit; user_identity shows the caller. Docs describe the event as a notebook export.
